item.title: IGN can exclusively reveal the new trailer, key art and release date for Family Guy’s next holiday special, “The Peter Clause,” which premieres on Hulu on November 30, 2026.
item.description:
IGN can exclusively reveal the new trailer, key art and release date for Family Guy’s next holiday special, “The Peter Clause,” which premieres on Hulu on November 30, 2026.
“It’s Christmas in Quahog, and Peter and the guys compete to become the town’s official Santa,” according to the special’s official synopsis.
“Peter loses, and he can either process his disappointment in a mature manner, or give fans a memorable episode of Family Guy. Thankfully, he chooses option number two.”
The trailer can be watched via the player embedded below.
Series creator and lead voice actor Seth MacFarlane returns as the voice of Peter Griffin, baby genius Stewie Griffin, talking dog Brian Griffin, and Peter’s pervert pal Glenn Quagmire.
Also reprising their roles for “The Peter Clause” are Alex Borstein (Lois Griffin), Seth Green (Chris Griffin), Mila Kunis (Meg Griffin), Patrick Warburton (Joe Swanson), Arif Zahir (Cleveland Brown), and Mike Henry.
“The Peter Clause” arrives on the heels of Family Guy’s most recent Halloween special. The remainder of Family Guy Season 25 will premiere in early 2027 on Fox.
Meanwhile, Seth MacFarlane will also star in a Stewie spinoff, which has been confirmed for a two-season order.
MacFarlane is also busy with the Ted: Animated Series, which debuts on Peacock on December 17.
In related news, read up on how Ocarina of Time remake players were stunned after learning a Family Guy meme works to summon Epona.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Shadow Recompiled is an unofficial PC port of the 2005 Sonic spin-off, now with achievements and more.
item.description:
There is no shortage of classic games getting so-called "unofficial PC ports" right now. Previously, these recompilation projects were few and far between because they take a ridiculous amount of time to make. But now, with many modders using generative AI to help them code, they're being pumped out so fast it's hard to keep up.
The problem with this is that not everyone wants to play a game that's vibecoded, either for ethical reasons or due to concerns over the quality. After all, recompiled games are supposed to feel like you are playing a game natively on PC, so expectations are high.
What is the best Sonic game of all time?

item.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians showrunners explain how Christopher Nolan's blockbuster The Odyssey unexpectedly boosted the Disney+ series' viewership over the summer.
item.description:
A new season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians is coming to Disney+ in just a few days and the executive producers of the show are revealing that Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey just might have led to a ratings boost for the series over the summer.
I sat down with Percy Jackson showrunners Dan Shotz and Jonathan E. Steinberg at, where they revealed that Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster The Odyssey probably led to more people discovering Percy Jackson over the summer.
“We've heard that there was a huge boost in viewers during that period because everybody obviously was searching for The Odyssey,” EP and co-showrunner Dan Shotz told IGN at Lucca Comics & Games. “And anybody who didn't know about Sea of Monsters, [the second Percy Jackson book, which was the source material for the show’s second season,] found it. But it was kind of surreal, to be honest with you, to watch it.”
The second season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians sees the titular teenage hero take a distinctly Odyssey-like journey, complete with maritime adventures and mythical creatures like the cyclops Polyphemus, the monstrous Scylla and Charybdis, the witch Circe, and the tempting sirens, just like Matt Damon’s Odysseus in Christopher Nolan’s film.
Shotz said he’s enjoyed how the two opposing takes on Homer’s classic poem have led to some distinctly modern outcomes.
“My favorite thing is all the memes that are going around that are like, ‘It took Odysseus however many hundreds of years to do this and it took Percy seven days. So he did it a lot more efficiently,’” Shotz said. “It was weird to see all of these iconic things that we were able to play with and that [Nolan and his team] were playing with in there, and how they did it versus how we did it. So that part was really fun.”
For his part, Shotz’s fellow executive producer and showrunner Jonathan E. Steinberg said he’s excited for fans of Percy Jackson to see what comes after The Sea of Monsters arc as they dive into Season 3 of the show, based on Riordan’s novel The Titan’s Curse.
“The hardest thing to do was to figure out how to manage all of these new faces and old faces who are in new relationships and in new places emotionally and make them all as important as Season 1 or 2,” Steinberg said. “The way you're watching Percy (Walker Scobell), who was the new kid not that long ago, figure out how to be a little bit of an authority figure in this world. We've been very lucky to find people who have just kept adding to the palette of what this show can do.”
Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3 premieres November 20 on Disney+.
Michael is Global Head of Partnerships at IGNE, where he leads all 3rd party partnerships across games and entertainment studios, including for tentpole events lilke IGN Live, San Diego Comic Con, gamescom, and IGN Fan Fest. He's spent 20 years working in the games and entertainment industry, and his adventures have taken him everywhere from the Oscars to Japan to Buenos Aires, Argentina. item.title: Actress and cult horror favorite Maika Monroe has confirmed that she won't return as FBI agent Lee Harker in the upcoming Longlegs sequel, although she's not quite ready to say goodbye to the character for good.
item.description:
Actress and cult horror favorite Maika Monroe has confirmed that she won't return as FBI agent Lee Harker in the upcoming Longlegs sequel, although she's not quite ready to say goodbye to the character for good.
Speaking to ScreenRant while promoting her latest horror movie, Victorian Psycho, Monroe was asked whether she'd be reprising her role in the follow-up to Oz Perkins' 2024 nerve-shredding nightmare.
"Lee Harker will not be in this one," Monroe confirmed, although her response wasn't entirely straightforward. The actress briefly trailed off with an intriguing "I'll just..." before reiterating that Harker wouldn't appear in the sequel.
However, Monroe added that she "would love to revisit that role," suggesting that while Harker won't be appearing in Longlegs 2, the door isn't necessarily closed on her returning further down the line. It's an interesting development, particularly given how the original movie ended.
Warning: Spoilers for Longlegs follow...
Harker survived her encounter with Nicolas Cage's deeply disturbing serial killer, but her story was hardly wrapped up neatly. After discovering the truth about her mother's involvement in Longlegs' Satanic murders, Harker was left facing the possibility that the evil she'd spent the movie investigating wasn't quite finished with her.
Of course, the bigger mystery surrounding Longlegs 2 is how Nicolas Cage is returning at all, considering his character rather definitively smashed his own face to pieces in the original movie.
Would you prefer a Longlegs sequel or prequel next?

item.title: As the second season of World of Warcraft Midnight winds down, it's clear that The Venomous Abyss was a bit harder than it should have been.
item.description:
As the second season of World of Warcraft Midnight winds down, it's clear that The Venomous Abyss was a bit harder than it should have been. And Blizzard is taking the opportunity to make its next raids easier.
Writing via Blizzard's WoW Forum entitled 'raid encounter design in Season 3', World of Warcraft developer Limestone discussed the direction for the final Midnight season, including some of the nerfs coming to The Venomous Abyss nearly three months after launch. The focus here is on "reducing the number of damage events that could kill you or your entire raid with a single individual mistake."
In Midnight's latest raid, The Venomous Abyss, there were a number of abilities, even on Heroic – WoW's middle-tier difficulty – that would wipe your group if you messed up. On the last boss, Ula'Tek, for instance, there were these little snakes that would hatch out of eggs in phase two. They had an ability, called Anguished Cry, that would deal half a million damage to each player within 60 yards and stun them for 6 seconds. That is less than a geared player's health pool, but the stun meant that if a single instance of that ability went off, it would just chain and spiral out of control, leading to the death of you and all of your friends. And that's just one example out of the eight-boss raid.
World of Warcraft: Midnight Cinematic Images and First Screenshots
At least it seems like Blizzard is aware of the problem. In the post, Limestone says it went too far in designing punishing encounters.
"We feel that our design has shifted over time at the expense of the average Mythic player’s experience," Limestone wrote. "Going forward into Season 3, we’d like to intentionally pull back on some of these severe mechanical penalties, even at the start of the season."
The alternative that Blizzard is pitching is that each mistake will be less punishing, but can still spiral out of control. As Limestone stated, "for example, a small missile landing on a character should generally not kill an appropriately geared character from 100% HP. However, if every player in the raid collectively ignores Malacrass’ cast of Eternal Nightfall, he will eventually complete his cast and destroy the raid."
The goal, instead, is to make the successes and failures of raiding a little less binary. Rather than one player messing up a single mechanic and killing 20 people, there will be "fewer wipes that feel like “instant death” and more wipes that feel like a slow unraveling as the group makes mistakes and productively learns from them."
This isn't the first time that Blizzard has had to dial back difficulty in Mythic raiding, and it probably won't be the last. Even back in The War Within, Season 2's Liberation of Undermine raid was a huge step back in difficulty compared to Season 1's Nerub'ar Palace, which Blizzard then corrected with Season 3's Manaforge Omega, which will probably go down in history as one of the best raids of all time. Hopefully Midnight's next raid finds some middle ground once again.
The retail team is probably feeling some added pressure, too, thanks to WoW Forever. I know that I've taken a break from grinding Mythic+ dungeons and raiding in favor of leveling a new Mage on the Classic+ mode, and I know I'm not alone. Hopefully, when the final season of Midnight launches, it feels good enough that it sinks its claws back into me.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?

item.title: Arion Kurtaj, 21, pleads guilty to cybercrimes related to the 2022 Rockstar hack and GTA 6 leaks.
item.description:
Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who first revealed Lucia to the world, has pleaded guilty to cybercrimes in relation to his 2022 hack of Rockstar. He also pleaded guilty to attempting to extort Rockstar, and to attacking workers at a facility where he was being detained after the hack.
Kurtaj, who is now 21, was 17 when he was initially taken into custody over the 2022 Rockstar hack. As he is from the U.K., he could not initially be named as a minor. He was also deemed unable to stand trial due to the severity of his autism, and was instead sent to be held indefinitely in a secure psychiatric facility. Now, as reported by the BBC, he has been deemed able to stand trial and has entered a guilty plea.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
The 2022 hack resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw Jason and Lucia for the first time, as they held victims at gunpoint. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. Rockstar refused to pay Kurtaj's ransom.
Crucially, this was our first confirmation that GTA 6 would star a female protagonist, a first in modern GTA games.
It would be over a year before Rockstar finally confirmed this itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year.
It wasn't just the leaked material that brought attention to this hack in 2022, but also the method in which Kurtaj pulled it off. At the time, police were housing him in a hotel after he was apprehended for previous hacks, fearing he would be targeted by rival hackers. Using his hotel TV, an Amazon Fire Stick, and a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard, Kurtaj was able to breach Rockstar, taking gameplay clips and files.
Rockstar claims that the hack cost them $5 million to recover from. It further claimed that the Lucia reveal was being kept underwraps for the marketing campaign, something that Kurtaj's leaks spoiled.
However, it isn't just these crimes related to the hack that Kurtaj was facing. The BBC also notes that the 21 year old pleaded guilty to physical assaults, in relation to biting workers at the facility where he was being kept.
Kurtaj is awaiting his sentencing. It is unclear if his time at the secure facility will be taken into account should he recieve a custodial sentence.

item.title: Vice City is coming to NBA 2K27 as part of a massive crossover with GTA 6.
item.description:
Vice City is coming to NBA 2K27 as part of a massive crossover with GTA 6.
NBA 2K27's Season 3 update will arrive on November 27, and it's completely focused on GTA 6. The new update will take players to Vice City via a new park next to the city's park. The area features oddles of GTA imagery, including the Vice City blimp that has been flying around Miami in real life and a statue of Macca the Gator, a cartoon character in GTA 6. Additionally, the season's rewards pass will also give you access to a wide variety of GTA-themed cosmetics and items, including new takeover abilities inspired by the game.
As one might imagine, fans will also be able to rep the new Miami Heat jerseys that were created in collaboration with Rockstar Games. On November 18, the Miami Heat will play a real, regular-season NBA game as the Vice City Heat, complete with new jerseys and a never-before-seen court. It should be quite the spectacle, and one that you will be able to at least partially recreate in-game.
Season 3 will last for seven weeks, and players can actually get in on the action without buying NBA 2K27. If you subscribe to Rockstar's subscription service, GTA+, you will be able to play NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15. Anyone who pre-orders GTA 6 on Xbox and PlayStation is entitled to a free one-month trial of GTA+, so this would be a great way to put it to use. Starting December 17, subscribers will also be able to take advantage of free GTA-themed items and bonuses in NBA 2K27. Ultimately, it seems like NBA 2K27 doesn't have to worry about fans deleting their games in the same way Madden does.
This update was teased earlier this fall when NBA 2K27 was released, but 2K and Rockstar Games kept a tight lid on what would actually be featured in the update. It appears that this is one of the final marketing beats for GTA 6, as the game will officially release this week. (I know, it's as crazy for me to write as it is for you to read.) The game will have a regional rollout, meaning that folks in New Zealand will technically start playing it a day before users in the United States (unless you take advantage of some loopholes).
GTA 6 is available to pre-load right now, and Rockstar has already pushed out a couple of updates, which fans will need to download before they play the game.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: GTA 6 is finally almost here, and the world's biggest content creators are trying to figure out how to handle this behemoth.
item.description:
GTA 6 is finally upon us and it’s expected to be a cultural juggernaut that overshadows everything in its path. This includes other game releases, movies, and even upcoming holidays, such as Thanksgiving in the United States. Economists estimate a $1 billion loss in productivity during the game’s launch weekend, as millions of people are expected to take time off work to play Rockstar’s highly anticipated game. All in all, it's hard to overstate the impact its arrival will have.
“To me, every GTA feels like a generational moon landing,” said Mary Kish, the Head of Community Marketing at Twitch. “It's so big, and it's so prolific, and it changes culture and my life to such a large extent that it can feel overwhelming.”
However, there is one group of people that are going to be working non-stop for the next month: content creators. Typically, content creators are given games earlier so they can make all kinds of videos about the game. I spoke with some of the top YouTubers and streamers in the world, including in the GTA space, and none of them have the game. That even goes for a popular GTA YouTuber known as TGG, who has 2.32 million subscribers. He was exclusively invited to Rockstar North over the summer to be one of the only people to see GTA 6 before its release and became a primary source for anyone seeking information about the elusive game. And yet, Rockstar withheld the full game even from him.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
This isn’t common for a major AAA video game. It shows the lengths Rockstar is going to to preserve and protect its blockbuster, which has been guarded with a veil of secrecy for most of the last decade. Rockstar has been very calculated with how and when it chooses to show what it has been working on. The company has subtly sprinkled short gameplay clips and teasers in the final days before release, but that’s about it. There aren’t any YouTubers who have weeks of uploads banked and ready to go, meaning almost everyone is going into this game completely blind and on the same level playing field.
That has presented a unique situation for a lot of these creators. Everyone I spoke with made it clear that this is a game they are genuinely excited for. Although they have a job to do, they have all waited years for this moment as a fan. Despite the pressure to make content, they all told me they plan to take their time with the game so they can savor it, with some of them estimating that it may take over 100 hours before they actually roll credits on it.
A lot of preparation is going into this launch weekend. Some creators are hiring extra help in the form of additional writers and editors, while others are planning on making a spectacle out of things. Numerous streamers have rented mansions in Miami to not only do massive, extravagant streams, but also celebrate the launch with others in person.
Introducing the Midnight Launch, in celebration of the release of GTA VIExclusive prizes, game giveaways, merch, and moreIn Miami, November 18th-19th. Presented by HyperX https://t.co/fYk4LqHSZZ
Gaming peripheral company HyperX is teaming up with Gaming World Media to host a flashy in-person midnight launch event in Miami with fans and streamers. This is not something being done in partnership with Rockstar. It’s just a group of creators and a gaming hardware company putting their money together to do something special. According to GMW co-founder Jake Lucky, the goal is to recapture the magic of a shared in-person gaming experience.
“Essentially we are throwing a party for people who are just as excited for GTA as we are,” said GWM co-founder Jake Lucky in a statement to IGN. “[We are giving] attendees not only a chance to play, but also [a chance to] win their own copy, exclusive merch, and even GTA inspired collectibles to remember the event by. I just really think it’s important to bring back the human aspect of game launches that we have lost in modern times”
This is a big moment for Twitch itself, as GTA 5 has remained a titan on the platform for years. Users have watched around 9 billion hours of the game and 1.7 billion of those hours came in 2025. Kish kept wanting to stress that this moment is “akin to a moon landing” and compared it to a seismic entertainment moment like a new Star Wars or Lord of the Rings film. As a result, they need to make fans feel that on Twitch.
GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN
“It's our responsibility as Twitch to say, ‘How do we show up and give them the best GTA experience known to man?’” said Kish. “How do we make this feel reactive and interactive, not passive? Because that's not what we do here. And how do we make you feel like you can be a part of the biggest thing on the planet?”
Twitch is putting all of its energy and money into supporting this launch. Despite not having any official partnership with Rockstar Games, the streaming platform has created custom GTA 6-themed badges that will display next to users who are present for streams of the game during November. The idea is to give fans something similar to signify they were there for a major moment in entertainment history. The company is also giving out 10,000 copies of the game’s Ultimate Edition to random users throughout the month.
Twitch began making its plans “well over six months ago,” according to Kish. Once it became clear that GTA 6 wouldn’t be delayed again, the team began trying to make whatever preparations that it could.
“The GTA tsunami is going to hit us like a ton of bricks and we have to mentally and physically prepare everybody,” said Kish. “All hands on deck, every chef in the kitchen.”
However, despite all of the hype, there has been a bit of discourse in the last week or two before launch. Twitch streamers like Ludwig Ahgren have noted that regardless of how great the game is, its moment might be a blip given it's a single-player game at launch. He suggested that this means that the amount of fun someone could have streaming the game may only last a week or two, but also suggested that viewership might drop because fans will want to experience the game themselves.
Many of the people I spoke to pushed back on this, though. They think this is an opportunity for creators to separate themselves and show their creativity.
“I think you're going to see what certain content creators are made of,” said TGG when speaking with IGN. “I still make some content on GTA 5 single player. I know other creators still make daily [or] weekly content on GTA 5 single player [which is] 13 years old, and GTA 6 is going to be a crazy step above that. I think Rockstar is trying to slow people down. I think Rockstar is trying to get people to live in this world instead of rushing through the story. I think the content creators that lean into that will see far more success than the content creators that don't. The content creators that treat this like a game, a single player story game will be the ones that go to the bottom. The content creators that treat this like a world will probably rise to the top.”
“I think for most streamers, it's probably going to be like we're going to marathon the game, play it, and then that's probably it for most of them,” said Forrest Waldron AKA KreekCraft on Twitch and YouTube. “But I feel like there's a lot you can do, and maybe this is my YouTuber brain talking, but you've got Easter eggs, you've got challenges, you've got speed runs. There's a lot you can do, and especially in a game like this, there's a lot of different things, especially I want to do a fat Jason, fat Lucia play through where you don't exercise them at all and you just make them as big [as possible]. How does that affect the game? So there's a lot of content there.”
Of course, a game like this also means there are a lot of people hoping this will be their big break. Twitch is aware that this an opportunity for smaller names to break out. The platform has made it so anyone can earn money starting from their first stream, if that’s their prerogative. Kish says that Twitch is doing whatever it can to help streamers have the opportunity to succeed.
“I think that there will be people who will make a name for themselves, as there always is every time a major game releases,” said Kish. “I think about times in our history where a game has risen to stardom and then streamers have ridden those coattails not just because the game is good but because that streamer is freaking good and that game propelled them into stardom.
“GTA is going to be a golden ticket for [many] content creators. This is going to propel hundreds if not thousands of content creators to stardom that you have not heard before. There will be names that we will be talking about at Christmas that we do not know today because of GTA. It's going to shake out and we're going to be like panning for creator gold over the next 30 days.”
New creators aren’t the only people trying to achieve something with GTA 6 either. A bunch of extremely popular and established creators who focus on other games and niches are attempting to pivot to GTA with this release. KreekCraft is a Roblox creator with over 17 million subscribers. Up until this summer, he hadn’t really made any content around GTA. He had played the online modes in 4 and 5, but didn’t delve too deep into the story modes. Ultimately, he’s ready to shake things up beyond Roblox and is eager to take a crack at GTA 6.
“As a content creator, I want to do more than just Roblox,” said KreekCraft. “I want to expand out of that. And this is a good opportunity to do that. [...] Part of me is like, I'm so tired of Roblox. I love everybody there, but geez, the decisions they make, it feels like 2012 Activision Blizzard all over again. I don't want to go through this again.
“And then the games, I'm 29 and we're still getting an egg where you run forward and run back, run forward. And it's like, guys, I just can't stream this anymore. And thankfully I'm in a position where I don't have to anymore. And it's like, this is the year I'm going to start prioritizing my mental health and it comes in the shape of this.
The same goes for YouTuber Tyler Smith, AKA tdawgsmitty, who almost exclusively focuses on Call of Duty. However, he has grown tired of the franchise’s annualized antics and has decided that GTA 6 may be an opportunity to find something that makes him a bit happier.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
“Today, I sat down and brainstormed for four hours for [GTA 6 video] ideas, and it's like, whoa, I haven't done this in two, three years now because Call of Duty people just want the same thing over and over again,” said Smith.
It’s easy to be cynical and say these guys are just jumping on a bandwagon, but they have legitimate visions for GTA 6 that stretch beyond the first week of hype. It does seem like this is a game where they can break free of tired cycles and flex their creative muscles more. YouTuber Trevor Martin, best known as TmarTn, knows this well.
He also got his start as a Call of Duty YouTuber, with his main channel being dedicated to the shooter franchise. That channel has 3.2 million subscribers… but he hasn’t touched it in seven years. His last video over there was a review of 2019’s Modern Warfare, and then… nothing since then.
Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games
He pivoted to his second channel that had been mostly let’s play oriented for the better part of a decade. Although he still plays other games, Martin has also become a respected source for aggregating GTA 6 news in the last few years. He estimates that he’s uploaded between 800 - 900 GTA 5 videos, which have accumulated over 200 million views collectively. The decision to move away from Call of Duty wasn’t an intentional one, though.
“Honestly, it wasn't like a decision that I made,” said Martin. “When I uploaded that video, I had no idea I wouldn't upload to that channel again. I think I was really lucky in that sense that it was just super natural and it was just wherever my interests were taking me. Luckily, I had built an audience that loved the let's plays and the walkthroughs and things on the other channels. When COD stopped being fun, I just switched my focus.”
He noted that GTA 6 is a great opportunity for people to break out, whether they be new creators or established ones looking for a new direction. He noted this moment is similar to Fortnite’s release, in that it unexpectedly changed the content creation scene, but this time… everyone is expecting it.
“Obviously everyone knows [GTA 6 is releasing], so everyone's going to be grinding. But if you can stand out, I think it's a huge way to break into the space. I also think it's a great way for established creators to reinvent themselves. There's going to be so much, but at the same time, there's so much in the game to make content on that I feel like you can break the mold and you can do unique things and all it takes is one good idea and you can kind of run with it.”
With everyone wanting to get a slice of the GTA pie, there has been a noticeable uptick in AI-generated videos about the game in the run up to release. There are entire creators who believe this game is their golden ticket, but some of them are going to be letting AI do all of the work for them. Some of these videos have generated hundreds of thousands or even millions of views, despite not being made by humans. TGG was quick to note that a lot of these AI channels blatantly copy his and other creators’ videos.
Martin called it “scary” after seeing how easy it was for someone to easily generate a lengthy video with high-quality assets that he would’ve previously needed a budget and a team to produce.
GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Screenshots
“Those videos, they're pretty well done and they're everywhere and the speed that people can get those out,” he said. “When I watch it, I'm put off by it, but I don't know if other people, especially younger people, are. Because they look great. If you had effects like that back in the day, I remember I used to have effects on [some of my Call of Duty videos], but I had to pay a lot of money for somebody to custom make all these things in [Adobe] After Effects and really highly produce the video. And now it's just a short script away and you can have assets like that.
On one hand, I think it's kind of cool and the technology is amazing. On the other hand, I feel like it kind of loses the love a little bit. You know what I mean? It dehumanizes it. So as tempting as it is, I'm staying super far away from that. I'll stick with simple text PNGs. I don't think videos need that. I think they look nice, but I don't know. I'm really torn on it because I think it's cool, but it's also really concerning.”
Martin went on to note that these types of AI-generated videos excel in informational content. They can rip guides, articles, or summaries from across the internet and spit them out into a new video. As a result, he expects these channels to thrive in the short term with content that teaches players how to make money quickly or unlock certain items. But when it comes to long term success and players looking for more entertaining and original videos? Martin thinks they will “struggle” due the dehumanized nature of AI content.
GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Screenshots
TGG echoed these sentiments too, noting that a lot of these AI channels blatantly copy their videos.
“I would like to be optimistic and say that people will be able to tell who's being authentic and who's really had these experiences in game and is going along that journey with everyone else,” he said. “And I'd like to think they'd be able to tell the difference between those people and the people that are just riding the hype. I might be wrong. I probably am, but I kind of have to be hopeful that that's the case.”
With GTA 6 being a single-player game at launch, everyone is acutely aware this is only the start of this game’s journey. Although Rockstar itself hasn’t officially announced it, everyone assumes there will be an online mode released later, likely in 2027. After all, GTA Online was a cash cow and Rockstar appears to have laid a fruitful foundation for at least another decade of opportunities and experiences.
GTA 6 Jason Duval Screenshots
The core online experience may only be a sliver of what’s to come for GTA 6. One of the biggest things to spawn from GTA 5 wasn’t actually created by Rockstar itself. Modders created an extremely popular roleplay community that gained a ton of attention during the early 2020s, leading to world renowned figures like LeBron James, Travis Scott, and Kevin Durant all playing the game. Rockstar ended up acquiring the team behind FiveM, which created the modding tools that birthed this content.
Fans expect that Rockstar will utilize this team to build out an official GTA 6 roleplay community across PC and consoles, if not an entire modding system that can be used across platforms. Bethesda has been doing this for about a decade now, but Rockstar may have the resources to push this forward in all kinds of new ways.
“I think the future for Rockstar is going to be definitely in the [user generated content] direction,” said TGG. “I think roleplay has been a crazy explosion, and I don't think anyone quite expected how many people just wanted to live in these worlds that Rockstar is creating, literally live in them. But you're at a point now where you've got three different games in one. You've got GTA single player, you've got GTA Online, and then you have GTA roleplay. And I think the future of content creation has to involve all three.”
With all of that said, it’s clear that GTA 6 is not just a highly-anticipated release for 2026. It’s a game that will set the tone for potentially a whole decade or more when it comes to content creation. New internet personalities are bound to be created, new trends will be set, and as TGG said, it’s a whole new world that is meant to be explored and dug into. It’s the start of a new era and one that we can only begin to imagine the possibilities of.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Excited for Avengers: Doomsday? Well, Marvel has already begun teasing sequel Avengers: Secret Wars, which sounds like it will be completely different.
item.description:
Excited for Avengers: Doomsday? Well, Marvel has already begun teasing its sequel Avengers: Secret Wars, which sounds like it will be completely different.
While fans have a fair idea of what to expect from next month's Avengers blockbuster, Secret Wars is currently living up to its name as something of a mystery. By now, many Marvel followers expect to see Earth's mightiest heroes coming together to fight Doctor Doom... only for everything to end on an Infinity War-style cliffhanger, leading into next year's conclusion.
But how will Secret Wars follow Doomsday, live up to the expectation of an Endgame-level finale, and stand apart from everything before it? Well, by being a completely different genre and unlike anything audiences have seen before, Marvel has now said.
Avengers: Doomsday Trailer: First Look at Doctor Doom
Speaking to Empire, Marvel boss Kevin Feige teased that Secret Wars would be "a whole other genre of story" to this year's team-up movie. Joe Russo, co-director of both films, added that it would feature "a really unique world." Hmm — some kind of battle world, perhaps?
"The only reason to get out of bed every day is to take risks and surprise people and try things that have never been tried before," Russo added. "I think Secret Wars is one of those movies where I hope people will walk out of it and go, ‘I’ve never seen anything like that in my life!'"
While still a year away, it's fun to speculate exactly what Secret Wars will feature, as the finale to Marvel's divisive Multiverse Saga and, apparently, something of a soft reset for the MCU in general. Of course, Marvel comics fans will have their own theories on what will likely happen, though the MCU obviously puts its own twists on even the most famous comic book runs. Where will the dust settle after all is said and done? We'll have to wait until December 2027 for that, though thankfully Avengers: Doomsday will be along first in just over a month.
Avengers: Doomsday is set to premiere December 18, 2026, meaning we're only weeks away from its release date. Last week, we learned that Deadpool and Wolverine stars Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds have writing credits on the movie. Feige also debunked one of the biggest theories regarding potential connections between Downey's Tony Stark and Doctor Doom.
How are you feeling about the future of Marvel post Avengers: Doomsday?

item.title: Xbox has kicked off its marketing for the game it’s not allowed to mention in its marketing. Like the weird alligator-shaped Xbox recently announced, Microsoft is doing its best to get Xbox players excited about GTA 6 without saying the game’s name.
item.description:
Xbox has kicked off its marketing for the game it’s not allowed to mention in its marketing. Like the weird alligator-shaped Xbox recently announced, Microsoft is doing its best to get Xbox players excited about GTA 6 without saying the game’s name.
“Are you suffering from Vitamin G deficiency?” the new marketing blast asked. “Dr. XBOX has you covered.” I don’t know much about supplements, but there’s a real lack of vitamin G, T, and A over there.
For some reason, Dr. Xbox is DJ Khalid, and he wants to get you ready for “the biggest week in gaming.” What makes it the biggest week? No one knows.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
The website lets you put your name in and get a personalized doctor’s note to play games this week on your Xbox. Obviously DJ Khalid isn’t a medical professional, and there’s no gamer vitamin, so it probably won’t work on your boss, unfortunately.
“As their physician, mentor, and professional motivator, I am prescribing the patient take some time off to enjoy the biggest week in gaming,” the letter read after I put my details in. “I advise they avoid all meetings, highly stressful jobs, and unnecessary negativity.
“Symptoms may include: twitchy thumbs, controller cramps or release-date restlessness.”
There isn’t a single mention of what makes this the biggest week in gaming. That’s likely because Sony has an exclusive marketing deal with Rockstar to promote the game coming to PlayStation.
This has led to some pretty embarrassing misses on Xbox’s part. The first version of the GTA 6 TV spot failed to mention the game coming to Xbox consoles at all.
Microsoft did manage to muscle in a little more recently, with the announcement that you can play GTA 6 on the cloud. This means even people who only own an Xbox One can play GTA 6 if they stream it, which gets them access to the game at Xbox Series S graphics settings.
Are you disappointed that GTA 6 is targeting 30 fps?

item.title: Fox & Friends discusses GTA 6 ahead of launch, saying it won't be a good thing for "our culture and society."
item.description:
Fox News and video games — I am sure the very mention of these two things together is enough to send a chill down your spine if you are of a certain age. Back in the '00s, Fox was at the forefront of the campaign against games, whether they were deemed too violent or, in Mass Effect's case, too raunchy.
Turns out, all of these years later, not much has changed. Grand Theft Auto 6 came up on Fox & Friends over the weekend as we get into launch week, and we got the classics: misinformation and moral panics.
As one of the hosts was reading off some of GTA 6's gameplay, such as talking to NPCs and petting dogs — stuff that isn't exactly unique to the game — another host, Rachel Campos-Duffy, interjected, saying she had to "push back" against it.
"I really am gonna say I'm not thinking this is a good thing for our culture and society," Campos-Duffy noted. "But let's see what you think after it comes out."
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
The other host then continued to list the features in GTA 6, pointing out that you can play as both Jason and Lucia. Campos-Duffy piped up again when Lucia is namedropped, and says, "She's a hooker."
It was then clarified that Lucia is a "partner in crime" to Jason, but that you could maybe play her to go "straight," moving away from the life.
Are You Taking Time Off For GTA 6's Release?

item.title: Ever since Microsoft first teased its next-generation console/PC hybrid last year, there's been a lot of speculation on what Project Helix even is. And while that speculation is going to continue until Microsoft actually reveals the next-gen Xbox, the company has shed a bit more light on what we can expect.
item.description:
Ever since Microsoft first teased its next-generation console/PC hybrid last year, there's been a lot of speculation on what Project Helix even is. And while that speculation is going to continue until Microsoft actually reveals the next-gen Xbox, the company has shed a bit more light on what we can expect.
As part of its 25th anniversary celebration, Microsoft put out a special "Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine" that covered everything from the new Xbox Nano controller to World of Warcraft Forever. But the issue also had a huge story on "The Soul of Project Helix" where Xbox VP of Next Generation (that's a real job title) Jason Ronald gave a bit more detail on what Helix actually is.
Back when Sarah Bond revealed the partnership behind the "next generation hardware," she emphasized that Xbox was working with the Windows team to make the desktop OS "the number one platform for gaming." Ever since then, the assumption was that Helix would be something akin to a gaming PC. But in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, Ronald states clearly that "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games."
XBOX Series X25 Limited Edition Console Images
The goal, instead, is "making it easy, intuitive and instant to access my games." But while the focus is on creating a console, Ronald still says "if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."
It's impossible to tell exactly what Ronald is describing, here, though. Because Project Helix will be able to run PC games, there is a certain amount of freedom that it has to give users, otherwise Microsoft could unintentionally lock players out from parts of their game library, especially on some of the lesser-known PC game platforms. It doesn't sound like Microsoft wants to stop anyone from playing any of their games. Instead, Ronald said he wants to "remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."
In reality, the Project Helix operating system is probably going to be some kind of branch off of Windows 11, and is going to take some of the DNA from the ROG Xbox Ally X. As Ronald puts it, "The ROG Xbox Ally was really an opportunity for us to learn alongside our player base with a lot of these concepts and the ideas that we had: being able to play libraries from across multiple different storefronts, understanding how PC games and console games can show up together in a unified library."
I have used the Xbox Ally X a ton over the last year, and while a lot of the bones of a console-like experience are there, I'm not sure it'll ever fully translate to the kind of polish you see on the Xbox Series X homepage. And Ronald is aware of that, too.
"The feedback that we've gotten from players has fundamentally informed and altered our plans of how it actually shows up in a future console," Ronald said. "Players shared where we met the mark and areas we needed to improve or approach differently. So absolutely, we view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix – but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix."
The biggest concern for the next generation of consoles isn't really which operating system they're running on, or whether you can run Excel – the question is the pricing, and it's not looking pretty. While Ronald does try to talk around the prices, it still doesn't sound like Project Helix is going to be especially affordable.
Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 – Hands-On Photos
"It's definitely a challenging time," he continued, "but as a system and platform designer it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable." I guess we'll see just how "accessible and affordable" the console is when it actually gets unveiled – however long that's going to take.
It also seems like Microsoft is using the RAM crisis to justify the need for neural rendering in Project Helix, as well. When talking about price, Ronald says, "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that."
For the uninitiated, Nvidia's DLSS 5 is a major example of neural rendering tech that's actually made it to mainstream games like NBA 2K27 and Hogwarts Legacy. The idea is to improve visual quality in games by using AI to enhance images within the rendering pipeline. And it sure sounds like that tech is coming to the next-generation Xbox in one way or another.
My hope is that they keep it optional. No matter how you feel about DLSS 5, it does have a massive impact on performance while altering the way a game looks. Luckily, in the official implementations so far, it's been a relatively minor change, but there are definitely some modders who have pushed the technology to comical levels.
With the way that graphics tech is moving lately, there's no telling what Project Helix will be capable of until it's actually in our hands. I hope that Microsoft does go for an operating system that feels at home on a TV. I was worried that it would just lean on the Xbox full screen experience, and it just isn't there yet. At least it sounds like no matter how the OS feels to navigate with a controller, it's still focused on giving people finer controls over how the system runs. And if Microsoft plans to lean on tech like neural rendering and frame generation, that's going to be more important than ever.
What do you most want out of Xbox's next-gen Project Helix?

item.title: After years of rumors and speculation, Twilight and The Batman star Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's 007 movie.
item.description:
After years of rumors and speculation, Twilight and The Batman star Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's 007 movie.
Official 007 social media accounts confirmed the news today. Additional details about Pattinson's Bond debut remain unclear, but the announcement post did include a first look, which you can see below.
"James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "I'm deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team."
Identity Confirmed https://t.co/FCU5A9c1wk
Villeneuve also released a statement on choosing Pattinson to play 007:
"Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin."
The Hollywood Reporter shared additional details about Pattinson's casting and how the news was kept under lock and key in a new report. Contenders are said to have been judged on stunts, camera presence, and dialogue while testing for the role.
As the competition for Bond stayed behind closed doors, Amazon reportedly became even more secretive after actually making its decision. In fact, THR reported that, while everyone online patiently awaited updates, it wasn't until yesterday morning that Villeneuve contacted Pattinson to inform him that he had landed the part. Producer Amy Pascal reportedly called the runner-ups.
Pattinson has evolved into a Hollywood name that needs no introduction, but we'll break it down anyway. He first truly made a name for himself as sparkling vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight Saga in the 2000s and early 2010s. Keeping from being held within the romance adaptation box, he eventually started showing up films like The Lighthouse and Good Time. After showing up in Christopher Nolan's Tenet 2020, he went on to appear in one of the biggest comic book movie roles in history as the lead of The Batman in 2022.
Pattinson also has projects like Mickey 17 and Die My Love under his belt. This year alone, he's starred in Nolan's The Odyssey, The Drama, Primetime, and next month, he'll show up in Villeneuve's Dune: Part 3 as Scytale. Now, while shooting The Batman Part 2, he's casually picked up 007.
Even those who have kept up with all of the latest updates on Amazon MGM's hunt for Bond recognize Pattinson's casting arrives as a last-minute twist. Although the Dune and Arrival director was confirmed to helm the next iteration of film's legendary British secret agent in mid-2025, questions about who would adopt the 007 mantle have swirled since Daniel Craig stepped away from the part following the release of No Time to Die in 2021.
As unsubstantiated internet rumors throwing out names like Tom Holland and Idris Elba subsided, more concrete background details on the hunt eventually emerged. Callum Turner (One Night Only) and Jacob Elordi (Euphoria) were two faces talked about earlier on, with Slow Horses star Jack Lowden then entering the conversation courtesy of Gary Oldman shortly after. Finally, just last month, Amazon reportedly narrowed its search to a small collection of actors, including Lowden, Turner, and Josh O'Connor (Challengers). Nicholas Hoult (Mad Max: Fury Road) is also believed to have tested for the role (apparently One Direction singer and Dunkirk actor Harry Styles made a few calls, too).
Early in the process, Amazon was reportedly said to be looking for a "fresh face" to take over as James Bond. Then, out of the darkness came Pattinson.
When production for The Batman Part 2 was hit with an unexpected and temporary break, the actor reportedly took the window as an opportunity to test for 007. It was all the time he needed, and he apparently made such an impression that his deal offered higher pay for fewer films.
With the part of the eighth James Bond now firmly on his already extensive resume, what comes next for Pattinson is anyone's guess. Seeing one star lead two major franchises on the level of something like 007 and Batman isn't completely unheard of, but it's not exactly common either. The expectation thus far as been that Pattinson would likely return for a third Batman movie down the line, but with the DC universe currently facing its own major shakeup, there's no telling how that might affect his time as the Caped Crusader.
Meanwhile, Pattinson's newfound Bond obligations are also unclear. Puck reported just last week that the actor's contract included a committment to three 007 movies. It's too soon to say if those details will pan out, but we can at least finally say now that Pattinson is your new James Bond.
James Bond: No Time To Die Character Posters
Villeneuve's 007 currently has no release date, but with a lead nailed down, we hopefully won't have to wait too much longer for Amazon to share updates. Peaky Blinders' Steven Knight is writing the script. If anything is certain, it's that the internet will have a lot to say about all of this. You can read about what everyone thought about previous James Bond castings here.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Prominent U.K. politician Kemi Badenoch has downplayed parents' fears over the violent content found in GTA 6, and said she's more concerned by how long many kids will likely spend in their bedrooms playing it.
item.description:
Prominent U.K. politician Kemi Badenoch has downplayed parents' fears over the violent content found in GTA 6, and said that she's more concerned by how long many kids will likely spend in their bedrooms playing it.
It's perhaps a surprising stance from Badenoch as leader of the right-leaning Conservative party, though one that she said was informed by her own experiences with video games while younger.
"I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically," Badenoch said during a news conference today broadcast via Sky News. "I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter — I didn't hit anybody after playing those games.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
"I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content," Badenoch continued. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went outside to do something else."
The subject of GTA 6 arose as the Tory leader laid out more of her party's education policy, which calls for a cut in the amount of time children spend in front of screens while at school. Indeed, Badenoch announced that funds would be diverted from the U.K. government's school laptop budget to buy millions of physical textbooks instead.
GTA 6 is now just days away from launch and we have a pretty good idea of the adult content that will be on offer in Rockstar's blockbuster. Age ratings from around the world describe GTA 6 as living up to its usual expectations, with the ESRB in particular warning that the game features "blood and gore, intense violence, mature humor, nudity, strong language, strong sexual content and use of drugs and alcohol."
While GTA 6 is of course rated for adults only, it's fair to say that it's likely that millions of under 18s will end up playing it anyway, if indeed they haven't already begun forging their school sick notes in order to do so. Rather than pretend no kids will play it, Badenoch is perhaps simply trying to draw something of a compromise. Of course some younger fans will likely play GTA 6 — but no one should be mainlining it 24/7 in their bedroom, full stop.
GTA 6 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. For more, you can check out IGN's preview from earlier this year. You can also check out the recent leak that spilled the full track list for the game's official album, and why we're excited to jump into Vice City, even if it's at 30fps.
Image credit: Leon Neal/Getty Images
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod understands that, and changes the game’s 2D rain effects into a proper 3D weather simulation. It’s called Torrent, and comes from a Modder called CyanideX.
item.description:
Rain used to be one of the key things you’d look at when the next generation of consoles landed to see how far video game graphics have come. I still remember being blown away by the opening of Metal Gear Solid 2 and its rain-battered ship at sea — there’s just something about the tap, tap, tap of sky water that pulls you into a world.
A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod understands that, and changes the game’s 2D rain effects into a proper 3D weather simulation. It’s called Torrent, and comes from a Modder called CyanideX.
“Night City's rain is drawn as flat cards of streaks, so it reads as a sheet hung in front of the camera more than rain falling around you,” the mod description said. “Torrent replaces it with rain made of real drops, falling through the world in depth, lit by the city's lights and stopped by roofs, bridges and your own car.
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Images
“Storms get wind-blown mist, and lightning with thunder rolling in after it. It draws its rain in the game's own rain pass and hides the game's rain only where Torrent's drew, so if anything ever goes wrong you get the game's rain back instead of none. Nothing is saved to your game, so you can install or remove it whenever you like.”
Each of the 3D rain drops in the mod has varying sizes and speed, and they’re impacted by weather and catch the light from passing vehicles. Droplets that hit surfaces explode into a fine mist.
Vehicles also interact with rain and puddles, with spray kicking up from car tyres as they move through the rainy Night City streets. A fine mist kicks up behind you as you drive.
As well as normal rain, the mod also includes variations so there’s light showers and heavy downpour, as well as toxic rain. According to the mod page, it’s compatible with lots of other weather effect mods so it should hopefully slot in and work with whatever you’re currently running.
Storms are also included as part of the package, complete with lightning bolts and strobing clouds that light up your surroundings like a camera flash. The mod is set up to keep the effects as random as possible, so you’re never seeing the exact same weather pattern play out.
Players who are sensitive to flashing lights can tone down the strobing effects in the options, replacing them with a softer glow. Or you can turn them off completely. Accessibility options in mods, what a time to be alive. You can check the mod out over at Nexus Mods (thanks, DSO Gaming).
Would Cyberpunk 2077 Have Been a Better Game if Act 1 Had Been Extended?

item.title: The latest deep dive into Fable goes over the returning capital city of Albion: Bowerstone.
item.description:
Over the weekend, Xbox released a digital magazine featuring details on upcoming games. One of the games featured heavily is the long-awaited Fable revival, set to launch next February after numerous delays.
In a six-page spread, the magazine gives us a bunch of new details about Fable, including some returning features and new quests. However, the big pull here is that it finally reveals the full scope of the capital city, Bowerstone, showing us exactly how it will look 16 years after we last saw it in Fable 3.
As we can see on the map, Bowerstone will be split into three districts in the new Fable. Those districts are:
Butterfield Market: The centre of commerce in Bowerstone. Shops and stalls can be found here, and all can be purchased by the player.
Copperbottom: Home of the working class. Placed physically lower on the map, Copperbottom gets less sunlight and has become a hotbed of criminal activity. Reminds me somewhat of Bowerstone Industrial in Fable 3.
Bowerminster: Where you'll find the nobility, including the residents of Fairfax Castle — the one you could buy at the end of Fable 2.
On top of this, familiar landmarks can be found in these districts:
Fairfax Castle (returning from Fable 2, and sort of Fable 3)
The Old Clock Tower (returning from Fable 2 and 3)
The Heroes' Guild (returning from the first Fable)
Fable - June 2026 Screenshots
From this, we can see that Playground Games has mashed all the different Bowerstones in the original Fable trilogy together. We have the whimsy of the first game with the Heroes' Guild being attached to the city, the budding aristocracy of the second game with upper-class areas like Bowerminster, and an underclass in Copperbottom, as we saw in Fable 3.
Many of these landmarks will also be familiar. Fairfax Castle was a major area in Fable 2, as it's where the player is taken at the beginning of the game and introduced to the antagonist, Lucien. That becomes Bowerstone Castle in Fable 3, which is where the player is raised. Here, Playground says Fairfax has "never been this grand," and will be a constant looming presence as we explore Bowerstone.
Which original Fable game is your favorite?

item.title: GTA 6 is finally almost here. With the November 19 launch date just around the corner, Rockstar is preparing the game for its public showing.
item.description:
GTA 6 is finally almost here. With the November 19 launch date just around the corner, Rockstar is preparing the game for its public showing.
A new patch has dropped ahead of launch day. Rockstar hasn’t released any details about what it contains, but it’s the second patch to drop ahead of launch now players have pre-installed the open world crime sim.
The patch brings GTA 6 to version 01.002.001 and comes in at 602MB on PS5. Some users are reporting that it’s available now, but rollouts generally happen in waves.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
The patch is also live for Xbox users and is 1GB larger than the PlayStation patch.
The previous patch, version 01.002.000, was released on November 13 and took up about 1GB of storage space.
For those who have preloaded GTA 6 already, you can press Options when highlighting the game on your homescreen and choose the Check for Update option. If it says version 01.002.000, you’re golden.
There are no patch notes for the second day-one patch at the time of writing, but Rockstar is likely just improving performance and fixing last-minute bugs ahead of launch.
If you’re wondering what else goes into making a Rockstar game, IGN spoke to a former researcher who spent time with cops and crooks to make GTA as authentic as possible.
GTA 6 launches on November 19, and we’ve got the global release times so you know when you can start playing. This week, IGN interviewed Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick to talk GTA 6 expectations, Online, and what the next decade looks like. We’ve also got a report on the hunt for information dataminers are currently on following the launch of GTA 6 preload.

item.title: Marvel star Anthony Mackie has insisted he did not drop a big Avengers: Doomsday spoiler last week, when he appeared to reveal an unannounced character.
item.description:
Marvel star Anthony Mackie has insisted he did not drop a big Avengers: Doomsday spoiler last week, when he appeared to reveal an unannounced character.
In an interview with Entertainment Tonight, Mackie said he had enjoyed filming Marvel's upcoming mega blockbuster as it had given him a chance to "just catch up with everybody." Specifically, Mackie mentioned singled out his downtime with Shang-Chi star Simu Liu and VisionQuest actor Paul Bettany as particular highlights.
As Marvel fans will know, Bettany's character Vision is yet to be confirmed as appearing in Doomsday — something that many pointed out in response to Mackie's statement. So, in other words, why was Bettany around to hang out with?
The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday
Now, however, Mackie has appeared on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon to set the record straight — and insist that Avengers' production simply gave him the chance to visit Bettany on the separate VisionQuest production that was going on next door.
"Paul Bettany is my man, my homie, we hang out all the time," Mackie began. "He was shooting VisionQuest next door to where we were shooting Avengers. So, me being me, I steal a golf cart and pull up. I'm a pull-upper.
"So I didn't say he was in Doomsday, I said he was next door shooting his show. Just like Tom Holland was next door shooting Spider-Man.
"He was next door!" Mackie concluded. "He wasn't in the movie... I guess?"
Somewhat ironically, Mackie's claim is backed up by an actual Marvel set leak from last year, where an Instagram user somehow managed to get into the production area at the U.K.'s Leavesdon studios and film what they thought was a Avengers: Doomsday set. Except it wasn't — it was the Madripoor set that was actually used in VisionQuest, as the two productions really did share studio space side-by-side.
Could Vision still appear in Doomsday? Sure. While likely not a major focus of the film, it's easy to imagine the synthezoid dad and his two sons turning up somewhere, fresh from their reunion in VisionQuest. That series' shock post-credits scene even pointed to the Maximoff family being set on a path to Doctor Doom, as the Latverian ruler appeared to rouse Wanda from her grave under Mount Wundagore.

item.title: VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt.
item.description:
VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt.
Before its launch, VisionQuest was described as the concluding chapter of the WandaVision trilogy (which began with WandaVision, and continued with Agatha All Along as its sandwich filling) — so there was some expectation that the sorceress from both series might reappear. But, alas, she did not — and Matalas has now explained why.
Warning: Spoilers for VisionQuest follow...
The finale of VisionQuest sees the return of Joe Locke's Billy Maximoff from Agatha All Along, as he reunites with Tommy Maximoff and his synthezoid sort-of father Vision. This picks up directly from WandaVision's final scene, where Billy sets off to go find his brother aided by a ghostly Harkness, who has now left her physical body behind.
VisionQuest Images
While Agatha does not appear on screen in VisionQuest, Billy still talks briefly with her. Tommy even realizes that Billy is doing so, and makes a comment about his brother having an invisible friend — as Harkness does not appear to him (or the audience).
While it would have been great to see her physically (or spectrally) again, the dialogue is still a neat way of acknowledging her presence and confirming she's still helping Billy. But why not have Kathryn Hahn back for a cameo?
"We can't afford Kathryn Hahn!" Matalas told ScreenRant, acknowledging Hahn's absence. "First of all, the second you bring Kathryn Hahn into a scene, it's a Kathryn Hahn scene. It's really about Agatha, and in that moment of the reunion, it needed to be about Billy. [It] needed to be about Tommy.
"So you can't detract from the story you're trying to tell just because it would be neat to see Agatha," Matalas concluded, "and so that's really the core of it... It's got to be the story of these three characters: Vision, Tommy, and Billy."
VisionQuest then concluded with a shocking tease of Wanda Maximoff's return — just in time for next month's Avengers: Doomsday. Where will see the Maximoff family again, and could Agatha still return in future? Perhaps next month will provide the answers.
